transform_fix.defect: AttributePrefixUnbound — mapAgentTaskToExternal stamped flowable:type/flowable:topic/<flowable:field> without ensuring xmlns:flowable was declared on <definitions>. The modeler's web/src/canvas/choros-moddle-extension.js registers ONLY the choros namespace (associations: []), so a real modeler export never carries xmlns:flowable — confirmed by direct inspection of that file and of web/src/canvas/bpmn-modeler-wrapper.jsx (moddleExtensions: { choros: ChorosModdleDescriptor } only).
transform_fix.fix: New exported function ensureFlowableNamespace(bpmnXml) in src/core/agent-task-external-mapper.ts injects xmlns:flowable="http://flowable.org/bpmn" (verified against the already-working hand-authored seed processes under config/flowable/processes/) onto the <definitions> root. Called from mapAgentTaskToExternal only when this invocation actually wired at least one new agent serviceTask (idempotent — skips if xmlns:flowable is already declared with any value; additive — a no-agent-task or already-external-only diagram is untouched, matching the existing byte-identical no-op contract of the rest of the module).

error_mapping_fix.defect: Ложный 503 — deployBpmn classified any HTTP status >= 500 as ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE via httpStatusToCode. Flowable's deployment servlet is LIVE-VERIFIED (docs/test-reports/T-0058.test-report.json probe-a, an existing artifact in this repo predating this task) to respond to a malformed/unparsable BPMN deploy with HTTP 500 and a JSON body {"message": ..., "exception": "...XMLStreamException..."} — not a clean 400 — while the engine itself stays healthy (health check 200 throughout). That meant a genuine 'our XML is broken' case (including the AttributePrefixUnbound bug above) surfaced as a dishonest 'движок недоступен' 503 and burned 3 retries first.
error_mapping_fix.fix: deployBpmn now reads the response body on any non-201 result via a new safeReadJson helper (never throws — falls back to plain status-code classification on a missing/non-JSON body) and checks it with a new isBpmnParseRejection helper against known Flowable XML-exception signatures (XMLStreamException, SAXParseException, BpmnXMLException, AttributePrefixUnbound, XMLException). A match classifies the result as BAD_BPMN regardless of the raw HTTP status. BAD_BPMN was already in withRetry's not-retryable list and flowableErrorToHttp already mapped it to 422 with a human message — this fix only corrects the upstream CLASSIFICATION so real rejections reach that existing, already-correct path instead of falling into ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE. Any other 5xx (no body, unrelated exception text, network error) is unaffected and still surfaces as ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE/503 — genuine outages are not masked (covered by a dedicated regression test).

draft_preservation_fix.defect: Порча черновика — POST /api/process-defs ran mapAgentTaskToExternal BEFORE persisting the draft, so the transformed (flowable:*-bearing) XML was written straight into choros.process_definition.bpmn_xml. Re-opening that draft in the modeler then failed importXML() with an unparsable-content error, because the modeler's moddle extension does not know the flowable: attributes/elements this transform emits.
draft_preservation_fix.fix: mapAgentTaskToExternal is no longer called in the POST /api/process-defs (draft-save) handler in src/http/process-defs.ts — the persisted bpmn_xml is now exactly the author's XML (choros:* only) after lane/timer mapping (unchanged, out of scope). The transform now runs ONLY inside publishProcessByKey, immediately after loading the row and before lint/executor-resolution-gate/normalizeBpmnForDeploy/deployBpmn, producing a local `publishXml` variable that is used for lint, the agentRef-resolution gate, and the deploy payload — and is NEVER written back to the process_definition row (the publish UPDATE statement only ever set status/deployment_id/updated_at, confirmed unchanged and asserted by a new test that inspects the literal SQL to ensure it never touches bpmn_xml).

tests_added.covers: ensureFlowableNamespace unit tests (bare root, already-declared no-op, prefixed <bpmn:definitions>, no-<definitions> no-op, byte-preservation of the rest of the document) + mapAgentTaskToExternal integration tests using a NEW realistic modeler-shaped fixture (choros: namespace only, no xmlns:flowable — unlike every pre-existing fixture in this file, which hardcoded xmlns:flowable and so never exercised this gap): namespace injected only when new flowable:* content is emitted (not for no-agent-task / already-external / id-less cases), idempotent at the namespace level, respects an explicit prior declaration, and the transformed output still passes lintBpmn end to end.

deployBpmn body-detection: HTTP 500 + XMLStreamException/SAXParseException body → BAD_BPMN; no retries burned on a body-detected BAD_BPMN; HTTP 500 with an UNRELATED exception (OutOfMemoryError) → still ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE and still retried (proves genuine outages are not masked); HTTP 500 with an unparseable/non-JSON body → falls back to ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE without throwing; HTTP 503 with no body → still ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE; HTTP 400 with the exception-shaped body → still BAD_BPMN (both detection paths agree).

NEW file. Draft preservation: POST /api/process-defs persists choros:*-only XML (no flowable:type/topic/field/xmlns leak); GET round-trips the same clean XML; publishing does NOT retroactively rewrite the persisted bpmn_xml (asserted via shared mutable pool state across save→publish, and via a literal-SQL assertion that the publish UPDATE never sets bpmn_xml). Publish correctness: deployBpmn receives xmlns:flowable-complete + externalised XML with the dispatcher variable keys stamped. Regression: a human-only process (no agent task) still publishes unchanged. Error-mapping integration: a Flowable BAD_BPMN result surfaces as thrown HttpError(422, code BAD_BPMN) through the real route, and a genuine ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE result still surfaces as HttpError(503, code ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE) — proving the two fixes and the draft-preservation fix all cohere through the actual publish route, not just at the unit level.
